reasons.A: Closest movement and stance: flat, severe assertions, semicolon-joined parallel clauses and double dashes used as the passage uses them, with a period feel that stays only slightly on the side of overdoing it (to-day, who shall blame him?).
reasons.C: Right period diction and dashes, but long, flowing, hedged sentences (I venture to say, One does not blame the students) soften the passage's blunt, censorious stance.
reasons.B: Modern, even-tempered expository prose: no dashes, a colon-led list, measured concessions and a tidy summarising close, far from the passage's clipped severity.
